text:
ana: Ran an nsys capture for the kv/prefix cache scenario that regressed on master after the batching patch. putting trace here: https://perfetto.local/trace/abcd1234
matt: thanks Ana — short summary? what looked different vs the golden trace?
ana: Main thing: the kernel chooser is dispatching to the generic GEMM kernel for a bunch of short sequences (~16-48) instead of the quantized matmul-fast path. That shows up as long memcpy + generic kernels in the timeline.
jyoti: hmm that's the kernel selector logic that picks based on seqlen histogram + tile fit, right? could batching change distribution
ana: yes. Batcher now groups by arrival time and tries to create larger batches quickly. That increases variance in per-batch seqlen mix so the selector errs toward the safe generic kernel.
matt: do we have the nsys stack slices? any hotspot in L2 or memcopy?
ana: nsys shows elevated L2 miss ratio in the generic kernel frames. Also a bunch of small kernel launches that inflate GPU enqueue overhead. NVTX timeline attached in the trace.
perf-bot: perf regression alert: +18% p99 token latency in scenario "prefix-redispatch" vs 2025-11-02-baseline
sam: Can you paste the exact command you ran so I can repro locally?
ana: sure:
```
nsys profile --output=out_prefix_bug --trace=cuda,cudnn,nvtx --sample=none --capture-range=nvtx --nvtx-include=redwood.* ./bench_prefix_cache --model gptq-6b --requests 10000
```
ana: Also ran a perfetto export for event-level timeline: https://perfetto.local/trace/abcd1234/with-events
jyoti: Interesting — selector uses median seqlen heuristic; if batching mixes a few long and many short, median shifts and we pick generic. Maybe switch to 95th percentile or peeking the batch tail?
matt: Alternative: tweak batcher to prefer sequence-homogeneous batches by seqlen bucket (bucketize short/medium/long) before coalescing by arrival.
ana: I tried a quick patch locally that forces kernel selection to prefer fast-path if >60% tokens in batch fit quantized tile. That reduces p99 in the local run to +3% vs baseline.
sam: Is the prefix cache behavior related? evictions could be causing more long prefix recomputes
ana: yes — kv cache TTL param was lowered in the commit, causing more misses for reused prefixes. The trace shows repeated KV lookup RPCs and re-populating the cache mid-conversation. That amplifies the mixed-seqlen problem because cached prefixes produce short continuation requests.
jyoti: So two contributing factors: batching mixing, and reduced cache hit rate -> more short continuation requests interleaved. Both push selector to conservative kernel.
matt: Good root cause. What's the mitigation plan?
ana: Short term: revert the TTL change (rollback PR ready) and tweak kernel selector to consider 90th percentile seqlen when choosing kernel.
sam: Can we also add a sampling trace inside the batcher (simple NVTX markers) to quantify how often heterogeneous batches occur? That will help decide if we can change batching strategy.
ana: already instrumented locally; pushing a small PR with NVTX markers and a quick perf test. Also adding a regression test that simulates heavy prefix reuse and asserts p99 < baseline +5%.
perf-bot: CI perf-run queued: job 6789
jyoti: Also capture a short nvprof-ish microbench to measure kernel launch overhead per small kernel — helps see if merging small kernels into fused op would pay off.
matt: action items: 1) roll back TTL change (sam). 2) PR for selector heuristics (jyoti). 3) instrument batcher and run perf suite (ana). 4) add regression scenario and CI alert (matt).
ana: I'll attach the trimmed nsys flame and the CSV of kernel durations in the PR.
sam: thanks — let's sync tomorrow 10am to decide which permanent change to adopt.
matt: :thumbsup:
ana: noted. I'll post PR links here when ready.
